name: Isolated Hair Shaft Abnormality

criteria.description: Identification of structural abnormalities of the hair shaft by light or electron microscopy
Lack of associated systemic or syndromic manifestations
Presence of clinically visible hair shaft abnormalities such as fragility, brittleness, or abnormal texture
Positive family history supporting isolated hair shaft abnormality
Exclusion of acquired causes such as nutritional deficiencies or chemical damage

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hair shaft abnormalities confirmed by microscopy with absence of syndromic features and clinical hair abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic or acquired causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hair shaft structural abnormalities detected by microscopy
searchTerms: hair abnormalities detected by hair exam

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal hair texture (e.g., brittle, coarse, or twisted hair)
searchTerms: unusual hair texture like brittle or coarse
hair that feels rough or twisted

common.symptomName: Diffuse hair thinning without scalp inflammation
searchTerms: general hair thinning without scalp inflammation

common.symptomName: Hair shaft irregularities visible on trichoscopy
searchTerms: hair shaft irregularities seen on scalp exam

common.symptomName: Mild scalp pruritus without secondary infection

occasional.symptomName: Hair color changes associated with shaft abnormalities
searchTerms: hair color changes linked to hair shaft problems
abnormal hair pigmentation with shaft defects
unusual hair color due to hair structure
nail problems linked to skin issues

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding nutritional deficiencies
Hair shaft microscopy showing structural defects (e.g., trichorrhexis nodosa, monilethrix-like changes)
imaging: Trichoscopy revealing hair shaft abnormalities and irregularities
genetic: Possible mutations in hair keratin genes (if genetic testing performed)
No systemic genetic syndromic mutations detected
other: Negative systemic workup for syndromic or acquired causes

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic beaded hair appearance on microscopy
Sulfur-deficient brittle hair with tiger-tail banding under polarized light
History of chemical or physical hair trauma
Absence of genetic or microscopic structural abnormalities
Improvement with avoidance of damaging agents

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting syndromic involvement
Rapid progression of hair loss with scalp inflammation
Neurological or developmental abnormalities accompanying hair changes
references: Orphanet: Isolated Hair Shaft Abnormality - ORPHA:79366
